subject: [OrchidAI] Spike of 5xx/429s — investigating GPU backlog / retry amplification
messages:
From: Alyssa Tang <alyssa@orchidai.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@orchidai.com
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: sudden 5xx/429 spike impacting production — please help

Hi Ben,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood API around 07:45 PST this morning. Latency has climbed from ~120ms p50 to multiple-second tails and several customer requests are timing out and retrying. Our logs show a lot of concurrent retries (client-side) which I suspect is amplifying load.

Key notes: 
- 07:45–08:05: 5xx rate jumped from 0.2% -> ~8% (mainly 5xx and some 429).
- We saw many requests to the long-context model endpoint, and our queue length on our side spiked.
- Support ticket #ORCH-1120 created by our ops team.

Can you confirm whether there is an ongoing capacity problem (autoscaling lag) or node-level failures? We need a short mitigation path — even a temporary fallback to a smaller model or rate limit would help while we investigate. This is affecting two of our revenue-critical features.

Attached: screenshot of the customer-facing error surface and a cropped traces export.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Customer Ops | OrchidAI

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Urgent: sudden 5xx/429 spike impacting production — triage notes

Ben/Laura/Alyssa — quick triage from runtime: 

Findings (08:30–08:38 PST):
- GPU serving pool for the us-west-2 long-context fleet hit 100% allocation around 07:42. Several ephemeral nodes showed high OOM/eviction rates.
- Autoscaler fired scale-up events but there was a ~50–70s provisioning lag for the larger instance types (cold-starts + driver warmup). During the lag window, the request queue length ballooned.
- Request-level logs show retries with short backoffs from a subset of clients; the retry burst materially increased effective concurrency and pushed queue depth beyond per-node queueing thresholds.
- Crash-looped model shards on 2 nodes produced elevated 5xx counts; in combination these created transient 5xx bursts and some 429s as the runtime returned overloaded responses.

Immediate mitigations executed at 08:34: 
- Enabled temporary fallback routing for OrchidAI to the 8k-context variant (lower mem) to reduce allocation pressure.
- Raised soft rate-limits at the tenant-route level for 60s to smooth incoming retries.
- Manually added two warm spare instances to the long-context pool and pinned them to avoid eviction.

Result: 5xx rate began to decline by 08:47 and p50 latency recovered toward baseline by ~09:05, but tails remain elevated. We're continuing to monitor.

Request for OrchidAI: please hold aggressive client-side retries for ~10 minutes to let the autoscaler and fallback converge; if you can widen retry backoffs we'll see faster stabilization.

I've attached the scraped pool metrics for the window (pool_metrics_20261105.csv) and a short Grafana snapshot.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Runtime Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference

Team — looping in leadership and logging this as an exec-level incident due to customer business impact. Summary for leadership: 

- Impact: OrchidAI production feature degraded; customers saw elevated 5xx/429 and timeouts between 07:45–09:15 PST.
- Cause (probable): GPU pool saturation + autoscaler provisioning lag + retry amplification from client retries.
- Mitigation taken: temporary fallback routing to lower-memory model, tenant-level soft rate-limit, manual warm spares added. 5xxs declined but tails still elevated.

As asks:
1) Options for a short-term concessions/credits discussion with OrchidAI (Ben — can you lead on customer comms and propose credit level?).
2) Platform change: reduce cold-start time for large instances or add warm pool capacity for long-context models (Karthik — ETA and blockers?).
3) Operational: create a playbook for retry-amplification incidents so support can enact rate-limits and fallbacks quickly (Laura/Stephanie to own).

Alyssa — apologies for the impact. We're treating this seriously and will provide a written incident summary within 24 hours.

Marissa Cole

Alyssa — following up with a short incident resolution and next steps: 

What we did: 
- Identified GPU pool exhaustion + autoscaler lag + client retry amplification as the primary drivers.
- Applied fallback routing and tenant rate-limits; added warm spares; patched two nodes that were crash-looping.
- Monitored and validated traffic stabilization across the 08:30–09:30 window.

Current status: 
- Traffic is stable and error rates back to baseline as of 09:10 PST on 11/05. No further 5xx bursts observed in the 24h following mitigation.

Immediate follow-ups (owner/ETA):
- Runtime: reduce cold-starts for large instance types / provision a small warm pool for long-context models (Karthik / 3w investigation + R&D ticket).
- Support & Ops: formal retry-amplification playbook and tenant-level quick-controls (Laura/Stephanie / 1w).
- Commercial: Ben to send proposed credit offer and a short technical RCA (Ben / today EOD).
